question: Where can I get renewable curtailment and redispatch volumes in Germany, by zone or node and by period?

answer.summary: SMARD publishes monthly renewable and conventional redispatch reductions by energy source and Bundesland from July 2022 in a downloadable CSV. The four TSOs publish event records; FfE maps some affected assets or clusters to daily events. Complete renewable volumes at electrical nodes remain unverified, and historical publication definitions changed.
main_caveats: A Bundesland in SMARD locates affected generation, not necessarily the network bottleneck.
The shared SMARD CSV is headerless and includes many unrelated chart series; the chart HTML supplies field order.
Before October 2021, renewable feed-in management is absent from the TSO redispatch archive; the 2021–2023 TSO publication has a further balancing-related gap.
FfE points can represent clusters, not each generator or the bottleneck; its tested event table ended on 2025-11-01.
SMARD data are revised; chart display limits and raw CSV dates can differ.

steps: Download the headerless semicolon-separated CSV and open the chart page HTML.

The chart page maps s-nepm_baet-1-1 to reductions in Baden-Württemberg and gives its ordered series labels: Wind Offshore, Wind Onshore, Braunkohle, Photovoltaik, Steinkohle, Erdgas, Kernenergie, Biomasse, Pumpspeicher, Wasserkraft, Sonstige Erneuerbare, Sonstige Konventionelle, Unbekannt (z.B Börse).
Each row starts with series identifier and month, then one field per technology in that order; 2022-08-01 has 0.01 GWh photovoltaic, 0.0 GWh wind onshore and 1.28 GWh nuclear.

The chart page lists 16 reduction and 16 increase chart IDs with a matching state title; obtain the mapping and category order from that page rather than treating identifiers as documented stable codes.
reading_traps: Rows have no header and can omit trailing empty fields; preserve positions and do not convert missing values automatically to zero.
The checked raw Baden-Württemberg reduction series has 47 rows from July 2022 to July 2026; the page configuration applies limit_until 2026-06-01, so raw and displayed date ranges can differ.
State refers to the affected generation, not necessarily the location of the underlying network bottleneck.
Renewable technology categories are separate from conventional types. Offshore, cross-border, and unknown values require source-specific interpretation.
SMARD can revise earlier periods after settlement.

The 2015–2021 historical reporting treated renewable Einspeisemanagement separately; the SMARD historical page states it was fully included in market-plant redispatch from 2022: https://www.smard.de/page/home/topic-article/46/217842/entwicklung-des-netzengpassmanagements
A later national Q2 2026 report, published 2026-10-12, reports 2,102 GWh renewable reductions: https://www.smard.de/page/en/topic-article/5892/221970/volume-down-costs-up-slightly

steps: Download XLSX and open Tabelle 7 for annual technology totals or Tabelle 8 for annual state totals.
Read column E as category, G as reduction and I as increase, with units GWh in each table title.
Use Tabelle 2 for the historical reporting break; preserve its quarter and measure definitions.

For historical feed-in-management lost energy (including certain CHP and gas installations), open https://bundesnetzagentur.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/DE/Sachgebiete/Energie/Unternehmen_Institutionen/Versorgungssicherheit/Engpassmanagement/Zahlen%20Ganzes%20Jahr2021.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=1 at printed page 20, Tabelle 12 for states, and page 25, Tabelle 17 for the four control zones; TenneT 2021 is 4.545 GWh and 50Hertz is 1.168 GWh.

For Q1 2022 feed-in-management lost energy, open https://www.bundesnetzagentur.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/DE/Sachgebiete/Energie/Unternehmen_Institutionen/Versorgungssicherheit/Engpassmanagement/QuartalszahlenQ1in2022.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=3 printed page 20 Tabelle 12: Niedersachsen 1.668 GWh; page 25 gives control-zone distribution.

For Q2 2022, https://www.bundesnetzagentur.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/DE/Sachgebiete/Energie/Unternehmen_Institutionen/Versorgungssicherheit/Engpassmanagement/QuartalszahlenQ2in2022.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=3 Tabelle 17, p. 25 reports TenneT 1.568 GWh and 50Hertz 548 GWh; Tabelle 12 breaks the quarter down by state.
reading_traps: Tabelle 7 separates technologies nationally and Tabelle 8 separates states; these are not a state-by-technology joint table.
Table 2 says EinsMan is integrated into Redispatch from Q3 2022 in this reporting series; this is different from the 2021 legal transition.
The file contains formulas and raw floating point figures; display rounding can differ.
The 2021 report labels control zones by the location of curtailed generation, not necessarily the requesting TSO. The 2021 and 2022 reporting regimes differ.
Historical Einspeisemanagement totals can include CHP and mine/sewage gas, not only renewables; technology-specific figures are in separate tables.

Use RICHTUNG, GESAMTE_ARBEIT_MWH, ANWEISENDER_UENB, ANFORDERNDER_UENB, BETROFFENE_ANLAGE, PRIMAERENERGIEART and timestamps for event aggregation.

how_to_use.example_result: Point: 50H_AVA_CR_FOE; Erneuerbar; Sachsen-Anhalt; 11.625000000000057, 51.90900000000005. Event: 2024-01-25 09:45:00–16:45:00 UTC; 1662 MWh; 50Hertz; TenneT DE.
steps: Query the map layer for points and the event layer for records; both use betroffeneanlage.
The demonstrated filter 50H_AVA_CR_FOE returns the example event; join on betroffeneanlage and verify operator or duplicate identifiers as needed.
Filter primaerenergieart for Erneuerbar and richtung for reductions; use beginndatum, endedatum, time zones, and gesamtearbeitmwh.
The map layer metadata reports maximum 2,000 features per request and the event layer 1,000; paginate larger event results.
reading_traps: The point represents an affected asset or cluster, not necessarily the physical bottleneck or each individual generator. Location assignment method and positional accuracy have not been independently verified.
Three of 418 point-layer records have no geometry: Börse (Amprion, twice) and EGM_DTS (Amprion).
Of 415 points, three lie outside a coarse Germany bounding box: Kühtai 2 (Uniper) and two OWP Deutsche Bucht records; offshore and foreign locations make a bounding box an imperfect country test.
Only a single name join was checked; ambiguous names, missing geometry and event-to-point completeness require further verification.
Latest event start returned by descending query was 2025-11-01, although the check was in November 2026.
Of 390 geocoded records declaring a state, all 390 fall within that state polygon from the same FfE web map; this is not independent confirmation of point accuracy.

if_unstructured.summary: Quarterly reports supply national quantities but do not establish a complete nodal series. Do not infer nodes or missing zone-by-technology cells from national totals.
recipe: Open the quarterly report and locate the generation-adjustment paragraph.
Record the quarter, units, renewable reductions and the separately stated overall reductions; retain the report date and revision context.
Repeat for each report; this yields national totals only and cannot reconstruct a complete nodal series.

For 2020–2021 feed-in-management lost energy (including certain CHP/gas) by control zone, extract Tabelle 17 from the 2021 annual report; the example gives 4.545 GWh in the TenneT zone in 2021. Record these as plant connection areas, not requesting-operator volumes.

For the first quarter of 2022, extract Tabelle 12, p. 20 of https://www.bundesnetzagentur.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/DE/Sachgebiete/Energie/Unternehmen_Institutionen/Versorgungssicherheit/Engpassmanagement/QuartalszahlenQ1in2022.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=3: Niedersachsen has 1.668 GWh. The report describes transitional balancing changes, so the series is not automatically comparable to earlier or later redispatch totals.
if_unstructured.location_method: The tested quarterly paragraph gives national values, not coordinates.
cross_with: Compare national aggregates against SMARD tables, preserving distinctions among measures and revisions.
